q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM frequents AS f1, frequents AS f2 WHERE NOT (f1.drinker = f2.drinker) AND f1.drinker < f2.drinker

counterexample: INSERT INTO Drinker (name, address) VALUES ('A', 'address1'), ('B', 'address2'); INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('X', 'address3'), ('Y', 'address4'), ('Z', 'address5'); INSERT INTO Frequents (drinker, bar, times_a_week) VALUES ('A', 'X', 3), ('A', 'Y', 2), ('B', 'X', 3), ('B', 'Z', 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 is looking for drinkers who frequent the same bars with the same frequency, while Q2 is looking for drinkers who frequent different bars.
counterexample_dsp: Drinker A frequents Bar X 3 times a week and Bar Y 2 times a week. Drinker B frequents Bar X 3 times a week and Bar Z 1 time a week. Q1 will not return any results because A and B do not frequent the same bars with the same frequency. Q2 will return A and B as they frequent different bars.
